newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom slips, dealers see no trading rule changes.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom slips, dealers see no trading rule changes.

text.p: Shares in Russian natural gas monopoly Gazprom slipped on Friday in early trade, and dealers said they were sceptical of talk that the giant's domestic paper might be opened up to foreign investors.
Traders played down the impact of reported remarks by Gazprom chairman Rem Vyakhirev on Thursday that Gazprom might open up its domestic paper to foreign investors.
The remarks, published in the Wall Street Journal Europe, helped boost domestic Gazprom shares on Thursday.
Gazprom officials told Reuters later on Thursday that no such changes were in the works.
"I think people understood it (Vyakhirev's interview) as a promise of more openness, but also that foreign participation will not be increased," a senior Russian analyst said.
He said trading in Gazprom was orderly, adding, "I see no more and no less demand in Gazprom than usual."
A trader said, "there is interest in Gazprom -- people still think its prices are attractive."
At 1115 GMT Gazprom shares had fallen slightly to $0.615 from Thursday's close of $0.627.
Gazprom's strictly separates shares for domestic and foreign investors and its charter has set aside nine percent of its capital for non-resident investors.
Only one percent of this has been issued in the form of American Depositary Shares (ADSs), which trade at a big premium to domestic ones.
The difference between the two kinds of shares narrowed on Thursday, partly in reaction to Vyakhirev's remarks.
Some dealers said Gazprom shares might be undervalued.
"Gazprom was the leader yesterday because the overall market was rising and Gazprom lagged behind," one trader said.
Sources voiced scepticism about Gazprom's announcement on Thursday that it intended to buy a 25 percent stake in Russia's biggest company by sales, national power group Unified Energy System (UES).
"It was just a declaration," one analyst said. "It is not an easy affair. It is too expensive to buy UES on the open market."
UES had slipped to $0.2285 from Thursday's close of $0.2315. --Mike Collett-White, Moscow Newsroom +7095 941 8520
